definition: Software that prevents unwanted web content like ads, trackers, and pop-ups from loading on websites, improving privacy and browsing speed.
metaDescription: Learn about content blockers - software that blocks ads, trackers, and unwanted web content to protect your privacy and improve browsing experience.
simpleExplanation: A content blocker is like a digital bouncer for your web browser. It stops unwanted elements like advertisements, tracking scripts, and pop-ups from appearing on websites, making pages load faster and protecting your privacy.
whyItMatters: Content blockers protect your privacy by preventing trackers from collecting your data, reduce bandwidth usage, speed up page loading times, and create a cleaner browsing experience free from intrusive advertisements.
technicalDetail: Content blockers use filter lists containing rules that identify unwanted elements by their URLs, HTML attributes, or behavioral patterns. They intercept network requests and DOM modifications, blocking matching content before it loads or renders in the browser.

examples.explanation: This popular content blocker automatically blocks ads and trackers on websites you visit, making pages load faster and preventing companies from tracking your browsing habits.
Safari allows you to enable content blockers in settings, which will block ads and prevent cross-site tracking across all websites you visit on your iPhone or Mac.
This DNS-based content blocker runs on your home network and blocks ads and trackers for all devices connected to your WiFi, including smart TVs and IoT devices.
